rationale: The stems, coordinate feedback, and paired-data explanation are clear for Grade 8, but the lesson repeatedly plots isolated points and never has the learner build or inspect a multi-point scatter plot. A cumulative table-to-graph construction is required so the visual establishes what makes paired observations a scatter plot, while the challenge should transfer beyond a third version of the same one-point placement job.
reopenCondition: Reassess after a synchronized multi-point scatter construction and a distinct transfer challenge are present; reopen on any lesson, course, duplicate-reference, standards-reference, figure, widget, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The opening fitted cloud and the positive, negative, and no-association definitions are readable and mathematically useful, and the context sort diversifies the final job. However, k1, k2, and i2 ask learners to infer graph direction from prose instead of showing the relevant plotted evidence; association is inherently spatial, so the question and explanation surfaces need actual varied scatter plots rather than descriptions of invisible dots.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the direction and no-association checks display accessible, synchronized scatter plots and preserve the varied context sort; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, figure, widget, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The scatter-fit canary gives a useful visible outlier and the concepts distinguish cluster, outlier, and form in concise Grade 8 language. Yet i2, k1, k2, and the challenge replace the very shapes being assessed with verbal descriptions; learners should compare plotted straight, curved, clustered, and outlier cases directly, with explanations pointing to the visible evidence and not only to memorized vocabulary.
reopenCondition: Reassess after every form, cluster, and outlier judgment is supported by accessible plotted evidence and a genuinely visual comparison challenge; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, figure, widget, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: Dragging a line through a visible cloud, estimating its slope, and revealing closeness, balance, and direction establish the central idea with accessible language. The later fit judgments are mostly prose-only even when a graph would be decisive, and k1 incorrectly suggests that a fitted line should 'ignore outliers if anything'; replace that automatic-dismissal message and show the candidate line/cloud evidence in the checks and challenge.
reopenCondition: Reassess after outlier feedback is mathematically qualified and all fit-balance judgments use synchronized candidate-line graphs with accessible descriptions; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, figure, widget, evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The opening scatter-fit state and direct wording make closeness and balance understandable, but the remainder asks learners to imagine Cloud X, Cloud Y, three described fits, a shifted line, and two candidate lines without displaying them. The lesson also alternates among gaps, total distance, and residuals without distinguishing an informal visual fit from the later least-squares criterion, so the visual comparisons and measure language need alignment.
reopenCondition: Reassess after side-by-side cloud and candidate-line diagrams carry the comparisons and the text consistently distinguishes informal closeness from a defined residual criterion; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, figure, widget, evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The rendered equation figures and affine laboratory keep slope, intercept, equation, and line linked, and the prompts and feedback are concise for Grade 8. The independent sequence nevertheless repeats parameter reading across i1, k1, k2, k3, and the remedial, while the challenge says 'read both pieces at once' but asks only for the intercept; diversify the jobs with graph-to-equation, error diagnosis, and a true two-parameter challenge.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the open progression repeat is resolved and the challenge assesses both slope and intercept through a distinct representation-translation job; reopen on any lesson, course, queue evidence, standards reference, figure, affine widget, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The initial fitted graph shows that a line can interpolate between measured points and the substitution explanations are clear. After that canary, i2, k1, k2, k3, the challenge, and the remedial repeat essentially one numeric substitution job—usually at x = 4—without asking learners to read a prediction from a graph, compare graph and equation, diagnose a prediction, or reason about units; a visual, varied sequence is required.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the detector-flagged repetition is replaced by distinct graph-reading, equation, unit, diagnosis, and transfer jobs with synchronized prediction visuals; reopen on any lesson, course, queue evidence, standards reference, figure, widget, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The line explorer makes the phone-plan slope and intercept visible before learners interpret the same structure in pool, savings, and taxi contexts. The sequence progresses from constructing a model to separating rate and starting value, interpreting each with units, and sorting phrases; the rendered figures, graph controls, stems, options, hints, and feedback are coherent, concise, and suitable for Grade 8.
reopenCondition: Reopen if the lesson, course metadata, standards or duplicate references, equation rendering, line explorer, generated choice behavior, feedback routing, runtime accessibility, renderer, or V4 review contract changes.

rationale: The extended scatter-fit view makes the measured range and far extrapolation visible, and the later jobs vary terminology, context, comparison, cause, and sorting. However, labels and feedback repeatedly call every inside-range prediction 'reliable' and say the rates alone settle trust, when interpolation is only better supported and still depends on model fit; qualify that language and preferably show the measured interval during the comparison and sort.
reopenCondition: Reassess after 'reliable' is replaced with appropriately conditional, evidence-based trust language and the interval comparison is visually reinforced; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, figure, scatter-fit behavior, generated choices, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The conditional-table laboratory keeps the complete table, highlighted condition, cell, and margins visible, and the lesson clearly moves through cell meaning, row total, column total, grand total, and category intersection. The challenge, however, repeats i2's column-total job on the other column rather than increasing demand; replace it with a missing-cell or consistency problem while preserving the strong visual table and Grade 8 wording.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the duplicate column-total challenge becomes a distinct missing-value, consistency, or interpretation transfer job; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, table figure, conditional-table widget, evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The visible table and denominator highlighting correctly distinguish percent of the whole, a row, and a column, and the language is direct for Grade 8. All assessed work reuses one 2-by-2 pet-preference table, while k2 and the challenge are the same percent-of-everyone job with only the cell changed; retain the visual denominator model but add a new table, reverse reasoning, error diagnosis, and a more demanding transfer.
reopenCondition: Reassess after the repeated single-table calculations are diversified across data, reverse reasoning, denominator diagnosis, and transfer while retaining accessible highlights; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, table figure, widget, evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The sampling-design canary and conditional table add valuable evidence about bias and row-rate denominators, but most association judgments are text-only percent pairs instead of side-by-side bars, segmented bars, or a highlighted table. The lesson also treats 70% versus 68% as enough to conclude little association without sample-size qualification and ends by claiming completion of all Grade 8 mathematics; both overstatements require clearer, bounded language.
reopenCondition: Reassess after rate comparisons are visibly synchronized, conclusions acknowledge sample size and evidence limits, and the false course-completion claim is removed; reopen on any lesson, course, standards reference, sampling or table widget, evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: The residual-gap and sign figures anchor observed-minus-predicted visually, and the sequence then varies direct computation, inverse placement, sign interpretation, a zero case, largest absolute miss, and comparison of two lines at one point. Evaluator targets, sign feedback, hints, equations, and options agree, while the vivid but short explanations remain understandable for Grade 8 and keep the mathematics central.
reopenCondition: Reopen if the lesson, course metadata, standards mapping, duplicate references, residual figures, plot-point or numeric evaluator, choice randomization, feedback routing, renderer, accessibility behavior, or V4 review contract changes.

rationale: The residual-plot figures and curved-data scatter fit contain the right visual foundation, but i1, k1, k2, and the challenge ask learners to infer organized residual shapes from number strings or prose, and the challenge explicitly celebrates working without a picture. Several statements also overclaim that patternless residuals prove the model captured all structure or that the relevant problems are invisible in the scatter plot, while metaphors such as diseases, X-rays, and screaming plots add avoidable language load.
reopenCondition: Reassess after each residual-pattern judgment uses an accessible residual plot, model-diagnostic claims are appropriately qualified, and figurative prose is simplified; reopen on any lesson, course, standards mapping, figure, scatter-fit or choice evaluator, generator, renderer, or V4-contract change.

rationale: This lesson teaches a learner-visible false least-squares result. For points (1,3), (2,6), (3,7), and (4,9), it calls ŷ = 2x + 1 optimal with residuals 0,+1,0,0 and a sum of +1 'essentially balanced'; the actual least-squares line is ŷ = 1.9x + 1.5, whose residuals sum to zero. The visual target, success feedback, k1, trade-off claim, and least-squares explanation therefore disagree with the mathematics, while 'all-zero residuals ... mean the data was invented' is also false and age-inappropriate.
reopenCondition: Release-block until an independent mathematical owner replaces the target line and residual set, aligns evaluator and all feedback with an explicitly stated fit criterion, removes false invented-data language, and verifies the repaired visual at runtime under a new review-basis hash.
